The main takeaway from our work is that

the democratizing potential of social media is limited by the fact that social media platforms are not themselves inherently democratic, and thus can be used by illiberal actors to undermine liberal democracy.

social media is not a panacea but a tool whose effects are contingent upon its use by political actors, and that its impact on political life in authoritarian regimes is not necessarily the same as that in democracies.
social media are not inherently democratic or antidemocratic, but are instead a technology that political actors can use to advance democratic goals or antidemocratic ones.
